summary: # Marvelous Designer: Hat Making Collection - Magician's Hat ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will walk through the process of creating a magician's hat using Marvelous Designer. This guide will cover the essential steps and techniques necessary for crafting a high-quality hat model. ## Creating the Base Circle First, we choose the **circle tool**. Click and drag your mouse in the 2D window to form a circle. Press the **Ctrl** key to create a perfect circle. The widest part of this circle should be twice as wide as your head. ## Positioning the Circle After selecting the board, click the **positioning key** in the upper right corner. Then, click on the virtual model to arrange this board near the head of the virtual model. The positioning symbol resembles a handle; now, the positioning ball is a double corner, as you can see. ## Adjusting Gravity If we directly press the Ctrl key to simulate, the board will fall on the head of the virtual model due to gravity in the 3D environment. To prevent this, we can return the gravity to 0, allowing the hat to stay above the virtual model's head. Adjust the gravity value to 0 on the right side, and observe that the 3D board will no longer be affected by gravity. ## Fixing the Board To prevent the board from moving, we can temporarily fix it on the virtual model. Use the function under the **fake needle**, called the function of fixing to the virtual model. Click on the board, then click on the head of the virtual model—this board will now be fixed on the virtual model's head and will not move horizontally. ## Creating the Hat Top Next, we will make the top of the hat. First, select the outer panel line and then click on the internal line border to draw an internal circle. When we select this internal circle, the double center point will retract based on the center. Adjust this internal circle to determine the size of the hole we are creating. ### Measuring the Hole Size When switching to the virtual model front, ensure that this hole is slightly larger than the model's head. Once finished, select the internal circle in the middle, right-click, and choose to cut and sew it. This will become the top of our hat. ## Positioning the Hat Top Now, arrange the position of the hat's top in the 3D space to confirm how high it should be, and delete any excess internal lines. You can also use the cut function directly. Since the board is now cut open, we can redo it and reuse the function of sewing to the virtual model. ### Fixing the Outer Circle We will fix the outer circle of the hat to the virtual model's head. Since the current 3D window is still set to zero weight, the top plate will float in the air. However, when the weight is zero, adjusting the plate does not apply our adjustments effectively. ## Setting Physical Attributes In the later stages of production, we will adjust the weight back to the original value to create a lifting effect. Switch to the **editor tool** and select the line. Double-click to measure the length of this entire circle, which can be seen in the attribute editor. ### Creating the Rectangular Panel Now switch to the **rectangular tool**. Set its width to the width we just measured, and the height to the desired overall height of our hat, which I set to 100 mm. Next, locate the **sewing line tool** and use line sewing to sew the panel sections in order. ## Adjusting the Bending Intensity Select the longest section, then press the **Shift** key to click in one direction. Use the "add to side" function to quickly arrange this panel near the hat plate, then freeze the top hat plate at the top. The entire model should now appear soft. ### Increasing Bending Intensity Use the attribute editor to increase the bending intensity of the material's physical properties. This increase will make it less likely to break and enhance its support. ## Flipping the Surface Since we are viewing the texture surface, we can see that this panel is facing backward. Select this panel, right-click, and turn the surface over to rotate it to the correct position. Click on the icon to switch to the display type of the panel. ## Sewing the Plates Together Next, use the line sewing tool to sew the two sides together. After sewing, this plate will hold up. Activate the top of the plate and sew them together, referring to the direction of the sewing line of the front and side plates. First, select the long side, then press the Shift key to click. ### Checking for Intersections In the 3D environment, check for any intersections in the sewing lines. If there are none, press the control key to simulate. We need to set the folding angle of the sewing line to create a folding effect for the nose. A straight angle when folding must be attempted first, possibly trying 90 degrees or 270 degrees. ## Completing the Hat Structure When setting 270 degrees, a nose corner is formed. Since we set the sewing needle previously, the hat cannot be removed. Use the edit sewing tool to select the sewing needle and press the **Delete** key to remove it. ### Finalizing Weight Settings Adjust the weight back to the original value of 9800. After starting the simulation, the plate collapses due to gravity, resting on the head of the virtual model. At this point, we have a simple fur hat. ## Adjusting Hat Angles We can now set the angle of the hat. With a 90-degree angle at the front, use the edit sewing tool to set the folding angle of the sewing line here to 90. After simulating, a sharp fold angle will be formed. ### Applying Fabric Properties Since the bending force is not particularly high, we can apply a new fabric to all the plates. Change the physical properties of the fabric to **Trim for Grain Leather**. This fabric has a high bending force and a low deformation rate, making it effective for maintaining our desired folding effect. ## Material Selection for the Hat Top For the top of the hat, although I originally did not plan to use **Full Grain Leather**, if a harder effect is desired, this fabric can be used. The key factors for maintaining shape are a high bending force and low deformation rate. ### Creating the Soft Effect If a soft effect is preferred, we can copy the fabric we just used, drag it to the top of the hat, and reduce its bending force. As we decrease the bending force, the fabric will collapse more. ## Ensuring Consistent Bending As the bending force increases, the material becomes harder. To maintain even bending performance across all directions for the circular plate, we can adjust the bending force of three materials to the same value. ### Finalizing the Hat Design When the bending force is set to 100, the fabric is not easily bent, resembling real-life magician hats. We can drag the hat to fit on the virtual model's head. ## Adjusting the Model Dimensions Double-click the virtual model to reduce its surface diameter slightly, allowing the hat to sit closer to the head. With the model in the open state, drag the hat, slowly turning it to fit. ### Final Adjustments If adjustments prove cumbersome, you can select all plates and rotate them using the positioning ball. Move the model's head to the center for proper placement. ## Finalizing Bending Forces Finally, adjust the bending force of the model and change it to ensure optimal performance. In my case, the bending force was adjusted from 0 to 100. ## Conclusion After all adjustments, we can reduce the particle diameter of all hat panels and lower the thickness of the collision. These steps enhance the hat's simulation and smooth the curves. ### Creating the Roll-Up Effect To create the roll-up effect on the side, we will utilize a **sewing needle**. Click on a point on the hat, then click on a point on the side panel to create the effect. Start the simulation, and the panel will automatically roll together. ## Adjusting the Roll-Up Freeze the middle panel to minimize the influence of the roll-up. Use the editing sewing tool to select the created sewing line, and in the right element editor, set the length of these sewing lines. ### Final Adjustments for the Magician's Hat Set the sewing line length to a high value, like 50 (5 centimeters), to create a natural looseness. If mistakes occur, more sewing lines can be added. ## Completing the Magician's Hat To finish, adjust the roll-up intensity to 100 to avoid interference from the fake seam. The magician's hat should have a high profile, so increase the height of the side panel, ensuring it maintains a T-shape overall. ### Final Touches Make any necessary adjustments to the sewing line positions or lengths, and use the edge curve tool to create curves where needed. By managing these details, we can achieve a polished and professional-looking magician's hat. Now, we can finalize the design with any additional details, such as trimming, creating holes, or adding decorative elements.
